citation: Ranes M, Zaleska M, Sakalas S, Knight R, Guettler S. Reconstitution of the destruction complex defines roles of AXIN polymers and APC in beta-catenin capture, phosphorylation, and ubiquitylation. Molecular Cell. 2021. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2021.07.013.
description: Biochemical reconstitution showed that APC promotes beta-catenin capture, phosphorylation, and ubiquitylation in the Wnt destruction complex. It supports the expectation that APC loss stabilizes beta-catenin signaling.

citation: Katoh M. Multi-layered prevention and treatment of chronic inflammation, organ fibrosis and cancer associated with canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling activation. International Journal of Molecular Medicine. 2018. doi:10.3892/ijmm.2018.3689.
description: This review lists AXIN2, NKD1, NOTUM, LEF1 and other genes as beta-catenin transcriptional targets. It completes the APC and CTNNB1 chain to the Wnt-target transcripts observed in the screen.

citation: Sato R. Sterol metabolism and SREBP activation. Archives of Biochemistry and Biophysics. 2010. doi:10.1016/j.abb.2010.06.004.
description: This review describes SREBP-2 as the cholesterol-regulated transcription factor controlling genes for cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake. It supports decreased sterol-gene expression as the direct expectation after Srebf2 loss.

citation: Zhao Y, Liang Y, Xu Z, Liu J, Liu X, Ma J, Sun C, Yang Y. Exosomal miR-673-5p from fibroblasts promotes Schwann cell-mediated peripheral neuron myelination by targeting the TSC2/mTORC1/SREBP2 axis. Journal of Biological Chemistry. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.jbc.2022.101718.
description: The paper links TSC2 inhibition to mTORC1 and SREBP2 activation with increased cholesterol-related lipid synthesis. It supports sterol-biosynthetic induction after Tsc2 loss and as the downstream half of the Depdc5-to-mTORC1 inference.

citation: Baldassari S, Picard F, Verbeek NE, et al. The landscape of epilepsy-related GATOR1 variants. Genetics in Medicine. 2018. doi:10.1038/s41436-018-0060-2.
description: The study defines DEPDC5, NPRL2 and NPRL3 as GATOR1 components and GATOR1 as a negative regulator of mTORC1 in epilepsy genetics. It supports the target-specific first step from DEPDC5 loss toward excess mTORC1 signaling.

citation: Moschella B, Busciglio S, Ambrosini E, et al. Genetics of Darier's Disease: New Insights into Pathogenic Mechanisms. Genes. 2025. doi:10.3390/genes16060619.
description: This review states that ATP2A2 encodes the SERCA2 ER calcium pump and that ATP2A2 mutations impair ER calcium homeostasis, promote protein misfolding, and activate ER stress and the unfolded protein response. It supports UPR induction after Atp2a2 loss.

citation: Waszak SM, Robinson GW, Gudenas BL, et al. Germline Elongator mutations in Sonic Hedgehog medulloblastoma. Nature. 2020. doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2164-5.
description: ELP1-deficient medulloblastomas showed loss of Elongator-dependent tRNA modification, codon-dependent translational reprogramming, and induction of the unfolded protein response. It supports an ELP1 loss-to-proteome-stress bridge.

citation: Liang FG, Zandkarimi F, Lee J, Axelrod JL, Pekson R, Yoon Y, Stockwell BR, Kitsis RN. OPA1 promotes ferroptosis by augmenting mitochondrial ROS and suppressing an integrated stress response. Molecular Cell. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2024.07.020.
description: The paper reports that human and mouse cells lacking OPA1 activate an ATF4-mediated integrated stress response. It supports the ATF4/DDIT3/CHAC1 amino-acid stress module observed after Opa1 perturbation.

citation: Galosi S, Edani BH, Martinelli S, et al. De novo DHDDS variants cause a neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorder with myoclonus. Brain. 2022. doi:10.1093/brain/awab299.
description: The paper shows that DHDDS encodes the catalytic subunit of cis-prenyltransferase involved in dolichol biosynthesis and dolichol-dependent protein glycosylation in the ER, and that disease variants impair this enzymatic activity. It gives a specific but incomplete bridge from DHDDS loss to ER and proteostasis stress.

citation: Dahlqvist J, Torma H, Badhai J, Dahl N. siRNA silencing of proteasome maturation protein (POMP) activates the unfolded protein response and constitutes a model for KLICK genodermatosis. PLOS ONE. 2012. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0029471.
description: POMP siRNA reduced proteasome maturation and, after prolonged silencing, induced CHOP consistent with ER stress and unfolded-protein-response activation. It supports a specific POMP loss-to-proteasome-insufficiency and stress bridge.

citation: Willemsen N, Arigoni I, Studencka-Turski M, Kruger E, Bartelt A. Proteasome dysfunction disrupts adipogenesis and induces inflammation via ATF3. Molecular Metabolism. 2022. doi:10.1016/j.molmet.2022.101518.
description: Mouse brown pre-adipocytes depleted of Psmb4 had reduced proteasome function, stress-marker induction, and compensatory Nfe2l1 activation. It supports a target-specific bridge from Psmb4 loss to proteotoxic stress responses, but not all neuronal transcripts in the screen.

citation: Waku T, Katayama H, Hiraoka M, et al. NFE2L1 and NFE2L3 Complementarily Maintain Basal Proteasome Activity in Cancer Cells through CPEB3-Mediated Translational Repression. Molecular and Cellular Biology. 2020. doi:10.1128/MCB.00010-20.
description: This paper documents that NFE2L1 induces many proteasome-related genes under proteasome inhibition. It supports proteasome bounce-back as an interpretable submodule after proteasome perturbation.

citation: Steurer C, Eder N, Kerschbaum S, et al. HSF1 mediated stress response of heavy metals. PLOS ONE. 2018. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0209077.
description: The study describes HSF1 as the master regulator of the heat-shock response and validates HSPA1A as a strong HSF1-responsive heat-shock target. It supports loss of heat-shock chaperone transcripts after Hsf1 perturbation.

citation: Trott AJ, Menet JS. Regulation of circadian clock transcriptional output by CLOCK:BMAL1. PLOS Genetics. 2018. doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1007156.
description: This genome-wide analysis describes CLOCK:BMAL1 as the core transcription factor pair coordinating rhythmic clock-controlled transcription. It supports decreased circadian-output transcripts after Clock perturbation.

citation: Guillaumond F, Dardente H, Giguere V, Cermakian N. Differential control of Bmal1 circadian transcription by REV-ERB and ROR nuclear receptors. Journal of Biological Rhythms. 2005. doi:10.1177/0748730405277232.
description: The paper shows that REV-ERB nuclear receptors repress and ROR nuclear receptors activate Bmal1 transcription through RORE elements. It supplies a direct circadian feedback relationship for interpreting NR1D1/REV-ERB perturbation only when the screen alters this module.
